answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. The effect holds because jury selection is secret and random, so an attacker can never target the specific identities that will judge it. This is why the network can stay open without a central gatekeeper: the economics of reputation do the filtering that a trusted authority otherwise would. Consider a haven as the anchor of the cost.
